# PR type
- [x] Bug Fix
- [x] New Feature
- [ ] Document Updates
- [ ] More Models or Datasets Support

# PR information

Refs #10483, refs #10312

With `dataset_num_proc > 1`, every `datasets.map` worker keeps one torch intra-op thread per CPU core, so N workers run N x cpu_count threads. Multimodal templates run the CPU ops of the image/video processors (`to(float)`, `sub_`, `div_`, `reshape` on the pixel tensors) inside these workers. With that many threads the cores are oversubscribed, and preprocessing gets slower than with a single process. The docs currently ask users to set `OMP_NUM_THREADS` by hand.

This PR:
- adds `swift.utils.limit_worker_num_threads(num_workers)`. It sets `cpu_count // num_workers` torch threads (affinity-aware), never raises the current value, and does nothing if `OMP_NUM_THREADS` is set explicitly;
- calls it in the `RowPreprocessor` map function when `num_proc > 1`, and in the `IterablePackingDataset` workers (`--streaming --packing`);
- updates the `dataset_num_proc` note in the en/zh docs.

Text-only templates are not affected (the tokenizer does not use torch threads). `num_proc=1` is unchanged.

Note: the map function is now wrapped when `num_proc > 1`, so the datasets fingerprint of these maps changes once. Caches written with `dataset_num_proc > 1` are rebuilt once.

## Experiment results

Environment: 20-CPU container, Python 3.12.3, torch 2.11.0, transformers 5.22.0, datasets 4.8.4. Length pre-pass (`AddLengthPreprocessor`, as run by `--lazy_tokenize false`, `--packing`, `--group_by_length` and `export --to_cached_dataset`). Mean +- std of 3 runs; main and PR runs interleaved.

Qwen3-VL-2B processor, 4000 llava-instruct-mix samples (~640x480 images, 388 tokens on average):

| dataset_num_proc | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 132.6 +- 1.0 s | 16.8 +- 0.1 s |
| 8 | 133.3 +- 0.2 s | 18.4 +- 1.0 s |
| 16 | 133.9 +- 0.4 s | 26.1 +- 0.3 s |

- Qwen3.5-0.8B processor, num_proc=8: 139.3 +- 1.8 s -> 27.4 +- 0.1 s.
- Text (Qwen2.5-0.5B, alpaca-gpt4-data-en, num_proc=8): 15.06 s vs 15.04 s (unchanged).
- The encoded lengths are identical (md5 of the `lengths` column) in every configuration.
- `cpu_count // num_proc` threads vs 1 thread per worker: 17.6 vs 17.9 s (np=4), 17.7 vs 18.2 s (np=8).

The remaining scaling limit (np=16 slower than np=8) is the per-job dill pickling of the template, addressed in a follow-up PR.

Tests:
```
pytest tests/general/test_dataset_worker_threads.py tests/general/test_packing_multiprocessing_context.py   # 47 passed
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD   # passed
```
`test_map_workers_split_cores` fails on main: the workers report 20 threads instead of 10.

AI assistance: Developed with the help of an AI coding assistant; benchmarks/tests run as described.

# Checklist

- [x] I have linked the related issue above, if there is one.
- [x] I have reviewed and understand every changed line, and I can explain how the change works and why it is correct.
- [x] I have run the relevant tests or reproductions locally, and included the commands and results above (if applicable).
- [x] I am responsible for the content of this PR, regardless of how it was produced.

+def limit_worker_num_threads(num_workers: int) -> None:
+    """Cap the torch intra-op threads of a data preprocessing worker process.
+
+    Every process starts with one torch thread per CPU core. When `num_workers` processes
+    encode samples in parallel (e.g. `datasets.map(num_proc=...)`), the CPU ops of the

+"""Tests for capping the torch threads of the dataset preprocessing worker processes.
+
+With `dataset_num_proc > 1`, every `datasets.map` worker used to keep one torch thread per CPU core,
+so the CPU ops of the image/video processors oversubscribed the cores (`num_proc * cpu_count` threads).
+"""
+import os
+import tempfile
+import torch
+import unittest
+from datasets import Dataset
+from unittest import mock
+
+from swift.dataset import RowPreprocessor
+from swift.dataset.packing import IterablePackingDataset
+from swift.utils import limit_worker_num_threads
+
+
+def _cpu_count():
+    try:
+        return len(os.sched_getaffinity(0))
+    except AttributeError:
+        return os.cpu_count() or 1
+
+
+class ThreadsRecorder(RowPreprocessor):
+
+    def preprocess(self, row):
+        row['num_threads'] = torch.get_num_threads()
+        row['pid'] = os.getpid()
+        return row
+
+
+SAMPLES = [{
+    'messages': [{
+        'role': 'user',
+        'content': str(i)
+    }, {
+        'role': 'assistant',
+        'content': str(i)
+    }]
+} for i in range(8)]
+
+
+class TestLimitWorkerNumThreads(unittest.TestCase):
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.num_threads = torch.get_num_threads()
+        self.addCleanup(torch.set_num_threads, self.num_threads)
+
+    def _limit(self, num_workers, cpu_count, num_threads, env=None):
+        torch.set_num_threads(num_threads)
+        with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, env or {}, clear=False), \
+                mock.patch('os.sched_getaffinity', return_value=set(range(cpu_count)), create=True):
+            if env is None:
+                os.environ.pop('OMP_NUM_THREADS', None)
+            limit_worker_num_threads(num_workers)
+        return torch.get_num_threads()
+
+    def test_split_cores_between_workers(self):
+        self.assertEqual(self._limit(4, cpu_count=16, num_threads=16), 4)
+        self.assertEqual(self._limit(3, cpu_count=16, num_threads=16), 5)
+        self.assertEqual(self._limit(32, cpu_count=16, num_threads=16), 1)
+
+    def test_single_worker_is_unchanged(self):
+        self.assertEqual(self._limit(1, cpu_count=16, num_threads=16), 16)
+
+    def test_never_increase_threads(self):
+        self.assertEqual(self._limit(2, cpu_count=16, num_threads=2), 2)
+
+    def test_respect_omp_num_threads(self):
+        self.assertEqual(self._limit(4, cpu_count=16, num_threads=16, env={'OMP_NUM_THREADS': '16'}), 16)
+
+
+@unittest.skipIf('OMP_NUM_THREADS' in os.environ, 'An explicit OMP_NUM_THREADS disables the cap.')
+class TestRowPreprocessorWorkerThreads(unittest.TestCase):
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        # In-memory datasets are mapped into `MODELSCOPE_CACHE`; keep every test isolated.
+        temp_dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+        self.addCleanup(temp_dir.cleanup)
+        patcher = mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {'MODELSCOPE_CACHE': temp_dir.name})
+        patcher.start()
+        self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)
+
+    def _map(self, num_proc):
+        return ThreadsRecorder()(
+            Dataset.from_list(SAMPLES), num_proc=num_proc, batch_size=2, load_from_cache_file=False)
+
+    def test_map_workers_split_cores(self):
+        num_proc = 2
+        dataset = self._map(num_proc)
+        self.assertEqual(len(dataset), len(SAMPLES))
+        self.assertNotIn(os.getpid(), set(dataset['pid']))
+        expected = min(torch.get_num_threads(), max(_cpu_count() // num_proc, 1))
+        self.assertEqual(set(dataset['num_threads']), {expected})
+
+    def test_single_process_is_unchanged(self):
+        num_threads = torch.get_num_threads()
+        dataset = self._map(1)
+        self.assertEqual(set(dataset['num_threads']), {num_threads})
+        self.assertEqual(torch.get_num_threads(), num_threads)
+
+
+class TestIterablePackingWorkerThreads(unittest.TestCase):
+
+    def test_worker_jobs_pass_num_proc(self):
+        dataset = IterablePackingDataset.__new__(IterablePackingDataset)
+        dataset._in_queue, dataset._out_queue = object(), object()
+        dataset.template, dataset.strict, dataset.num_proc = object(), False, 3
+        jobs = dataset._worker_jobs()
+        self.assertEqual(len(jobs), 3)
+        self.assertTrue(all(job[-1] == 3 for job in jobs))
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    unittest.main()

@@ -603,7 +603,7 @@ def test_packing_worker_job_carries_the_plugin_paths(self):
         # patch cannot reach them; the paths ride along in the job tuple instead.
         ipd = _run_iter_packing(None, _make_rows(4), template=CodecProbeTemplate())
         try:
-            self.assertEqual(ipd._worker_jobs()[0][-1], get_external_files())
+            self.assertEqual(ipd._worker_jobs()[0][4], get_external_files())
         finally:
